PROBE (b) REGRESSED real 72 -> 74, and it is the informative failure: `u8 *hn = (u8 *)c + j * sizeof(CritterHitNode); if (*(void **)(hn + (offsetof(Critter, hitnodes) + offsetof(CritterHitNode, active))) == NULL) { continue; } node = hn + offsetof(Critter, hitnodes);` gave the target's `add r3,r28,r27` and `lwz r0,1276(r3)` exactly, but emitted `addi r7,r3,1272` AFTER the `beq` and then folded the next two loads to `1360(r3)`/`1356(r3)` instead of `88(r7)`/`84(r7)`. PROBE (c) NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL: `s32 type;` moved above `s32 hit;` in the declaration list. PROBE (d) REGRESSED real 68 -> 74: `center[0] = delta[0] + c->pos[0];` and the two siblings.
attributes.residual: Four clusters, all one mechanism, plus a permutation. THE MECHANISM, seen at two sites: where the source says `X[0] + delta[0]`, the target loads `delta[0]` first and `X[0]` second while ours loads `X[0]` first. At @0x18-0x34 ours hoists `lfs f1,92(r3)` above `mr r28,r3` (reading the incoming parameter) while the target hoists `lfs f0,0(r4)` above its `mr r28,r4` instead; at @0xf0/@0xf8 the same pair swaps (`lfs f0,0(r28)` then `lfs f1,60(r7)` in the target, the reverse in ours). Both streams then emit the SAME `fadds f0,f1,f0`, which is why probe (d) -- reassociating the source -- moved the fadds and not the loads. The second half is a clean 5-cycle callee-saved permutation with r30 and r25 already fixed; savedregs prints `LIFETIME PERMUTATION: 9 live range(s) -- r25->r27 x3, r26->r27 x2, r27->r28, r28->r29, r29->r31, r31->r26` and `EMISSION ORDER DIFFERS: target r27 r28 r30 f29 f28 f30 f31 f27 r29 r31 r25 r26 / ours r28 r29 f29 r30 f28 f30 f31 f27 r31 r26 r25 r27`. All five FPR webs (f27-f31) already agree.

hypothesis.statement: The remaining residual is ONE mechanism seen twice plus a clean 5-cycle recolor, and the recolor is the bigger half. Every web below was read out of both streams by `savedregs.py` as a FIRST DEFINITION, not inferred: `type` is target `@0x94 mr. r31,r3` against ours `@0x94 mr. r26,r3`; `item` is target `@0x84 add r29,r3,r0` against ours `@0x84 add r31,r3,r0`; `c` is target `@0x18 mr r27,r3` against ours `@0x1c mr r28,r3`; `delta` is target `@0x24 mr r28,r4` against ours `@0x24 mr r29,r4`; `j` is target `@0xb0 li r26,0` against ours `@0xb0 li r27,0`. TWO ALREADY AGREE: `cpos` at target `@0x2c addi r30,r27,92` versus ours `@0x30 addi r30,r28,92` (same register, differing only in the base it reads), and the `@0xac li r25,0` web, identical in both. The one web out of place is `type`: the target gives it the HIGHEST callee-saved register while ours gives it the second-lowest, and every other row is that displacement rippling. Declaration order is denied above for `type`, so the next lane should change what `type` IS rather than where it is declared -- give the `fn_8005D5C8` result a wider live range (assign it once and read it after the loop) so it stops being a short test-only web that the allocator can afford to bury.
